*** THE HEADLINE DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED: DOORS DID NOT WORK AT ALL. sim.player.pos IS NOT THE PLAYER POSITION — it is a MIRROR. combat-bridge.mirror() copies combat.player.pos into sim.player.pos at the top of every step (the comment in Engine._settleWorld says so verbatim). useDoor()/leaveInterior() wrote the mirror, so a door taken on frame N was silently undone on frame N+1. MEASURED in the browser: enterInterior(archon-guild-office) put the body at the declared interior_spawn [0,0,6.6]; ONE step later it was back at the exterior [2766.5,0,5011]. And NOTHING WAS RED, because sim.env.interior was set correctly the whole time — every census-shaped check passed while the player never actually went anywhere. This is AGENT-PROTOCOL failure mode 1 (two parallel copies of one piece of state, system writing the one nobody reads). FIX: Engine._placeBody(x,y,z) — teleport()s list minus province streaming and camera settle, both unsafe under the armed guard and both resolving later in the same frame — installed as sim.placeBody and called by useDoor/leaveInterior. VERIFIED in the browser: body now holds [0,0,6.6] across 6 steps and returns to the declared exterior_spawn [3785,3.42,3791.3] and stays.

MY OWN FIRST PROBE PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON and that is how the above was found. Any consumption check whose delta is smaller than the perturbation is a false positive; the probe now asserts entered===true and compares against the DECLARED spawn rather than merely against inequality.

WHY A BAD NON-NULL SETTLEMENT IS WORSE THAN null, mechanically. RoadBook.forNpc is `RoadBook.settlementOf(npc) || fallbackSettlement` and engine.js rumourFor is `npc.settlement || npc.record.settlement || sim.env.settlement`. Both fall back to WHERE THE PLAYER IS STANDING when the NPC has none — that fallback is deliberate (topic-supply.js comments it: four people stood in Soulrest and none could tell you the way out). A non-null junk string SHORT-CIRCUITS the fallback: `"rootlands" || fallback` returns "rootlands", RumourBook.for() filters every row out on `r.settlement !== settlement`, bySettlement.get() misses, and the person answers nothing. So the 13 null-settlement NPCs are FINE and must not be touched; only the junk strings are the defect.

`rootlands` IS NOT EVEN A REGION. game/data/world/regions.json / settlements use `western-rootlands` and `eastern-rootlands`; plain `rootlands` appears nowhere in game/data/world/. NPC records also have no `region` key at all (336/336 carry `settlement`, 0 carry `region`). The three — rootlands-keeper (Hist grove rootkeeper), rootlands-drowned-speaker (Vakh), rootlands-band-elder (river-band ferryman on a bank) — are wilderness people, and topic-supply.js documents the correct representation for exactly them: "Returns [] for somebody who belongs to no settlement, which is correct: a hermit on the Clay Moor is not a signpost." So the fix is settlement:null, not a reassignment to a town.

`tidewrack` (jeeh-ei, warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma, clerk-avelia-doren) is LEGITIMATE and must not be swept up with rootlands: it has no settlement record but it DOES have a rumours.json bucket in both `rumours` and `race_gated`, so those three can answer what the place is saying. It has no road-directions `from` bucket, which is also correct — tidewrack is the opening prison barge and there is no road off it. This is why the check keys on `settlement records UNION rumour buckets`, not on the settlements directory alone.

CONSUMPTION PROVEN FOR THE SETTLEMENT FIELD, 5/5, against the REAL consumers. tools/world/w1-04-settlement-field.mjs imports RumourBook and RoadBook out of game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js — the same classes engine.js constructs — and wires them exactly as Engine._installTopicSupply() does. It runs in bare Node without an engine or a browser because topic-supply.js imports only core/topics.js; nothing in the probe reimplements the consumer. With the player standing in thorn and ONLY the record own settlement differing between the two runs: all three rootlands people go roads 2 -> 0 and rumour -> none when the junk value is put back, and so do widow-ineel and herbwife-ossa with `thornmarsh`. A control townsperson (rootkeeper-sesh-anaat, settlement=thorn) ANSWERS, so the run distinguishes `the field is consumed` from `the books are empty` — the probe exits 1 if the control is silent, if any junk value is present, or if any perturbation changes nothing.

CAPTURE FINDING, worth someone else knowing: tools/harness/viewpoints.json VP04-settlement-street — the one viewpoint named for MY piece — has `anchor: settlement_primary_street` but a hardcoded camera at [4,1.7,-6], i.e. the WORLD ORIGIN. The anchor is not resolved by anything. Shot through it, it renders empty terrain and sky with no settlement in frame. It is not evidence of a settlement and no one should cite it as such. Thorn actually stands at its record centre [3820,13.31,859]; shooting --at 3820,859 gives the stilt town. VP04 either needs its anchor resolved against game/data/world/settlements/ or its camera moved; not fixed here because tools/harness/viewpoints.json is the art-direction pieces file, not mine.

Thorn photographs as a stilt town UNDER a closed Hist canopy: at eye height you are beneath the platforms among the posts, and at eye 10-17 you are above the roofline in a field of canopy cones with the buildings hidden below. Anyone capturing a settlement here should use eye 1.7-2.5 and expect a dark frame with sky only in gaps — that is the architecture, not a lighting defect.
